steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: This is a report on the Shanhaizhong and Catastrophe countermeasures... and review of my own actions.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I'm sorry I let you down, Father...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Now, I will—

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You won't have to participate in Yumen's return to the capital anymore.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Are you giving me a suspension?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: It's not my place to interfere with the Sui Regulator's appointments, but as the warden of Yumen, I have authority over military personnel assignments.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: There's an important mission for you to undertake, away from Yumen.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: It's planting season in Dahuang, in the north, and they're short-handed. Go and help them.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Planting season? You mean, agriculture?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: That's the 'important mission'?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Is that not important?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I understand that agriculture is the lifeblood of the nation, and I've heard about Dahuang, but...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't understand. Why me?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: So you might see.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: And after I see...?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You think.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Be ready to depart, once you've completed the mission handover.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: One last thing, Father.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I discovered some suspicious activity when investigating the Shanhaizhong's movements.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: They appeared to be very familiar with Yumen patrol schedules and routes.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: If they really managed to obtain intelligence on Yumen's defenses—

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I have spoken.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: This is not your concern anymore.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Never forget what all you do is for.

steps.name: Jieyun
steps.text: A man like you can't be trusted!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Working in the fields by day and practicing kung fu by night for a whole month. You must be exhausted.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: *pant* Yun... it's you.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: You were focused.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But I didn't achieve anything...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...I don't even know what I'm doing here.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Perhaps, by focusing on improving myself here, I'll be able to do what I couldn't before.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Well... perhaps.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: You know, there's this old Lungmen kung fu movie...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The hero was an arrogant and haughty swordsman who spent all his life pursuing martial perfection, which always seemed just out of reach.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: His fortunes took an ill turn and he lost everything: fame, fortune, reputation, even one of his arms. Now a broken man, he found himself in a tiny, remote village.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: There, he lived amongst the peasants, eating with the lowly folk who used to lie beneath his notice. For three years, he chopped his own firewood and boiled his own water, not touching his sword even once.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: He finally drew his blade when his enemies came for him. To his surprise, his sword struck with a fury he had never known before.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Are... are you saying that I'm arrogant and haughty?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I'm just telling you what happened in the movie.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Do things like that happen in reality?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: To my knowledge? Of course not. The audiences love it, though. Back to basics, the proud humbled, that sort of thing.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: However, it is true that one's temperament has an effect on many things.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Have you felt your perspective change since you left Yumen?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't feel like it has at all...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: How about a break? Water?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Thanks. I have a question myself...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Why did you come with me? Why not stay in Yumen?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: You're traveling across Yan as Candleholder. I felt like I could learn a lot by accompanying you on your journeys.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I was demot—sent here by father. You could have learned just as much by going back to the capital with Yumen.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I went with Laoshi to Baizao. It was prosperous, but little else.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Dahuang seemed more interesting.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You're talking like you're on holiday.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't understand what Father wants me to see...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: What have you seen, then, during your time in Dahuang?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What have I seen...?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Dahuang used to be one of the rare places without much Originium pollution, due to its unique geography, making it an important Yanese breadbasket since antiquity.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But thanks to the hard work of the Agricultural Tianshis, arable land area is growing year after year.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Construction has begun on defenses against potential Catastrophes.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Currently, the city has sixteen large plates, some sixty or so small plates, seven hundred and thirty Tianshis, and a population exceeding fifty thousand.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Despite its remote location, the people are content and hardworking...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Is that all?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Just some insignificant details.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Insignificant, eh?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What about you? Did you find any sights that you couldn't have seen with the Grandmaster?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Well... for example...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The couple next door had a big fight after dinner last night.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The husband had gone on a journey last month and found the other cities to be much more interesting. He wanted to move away.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I saw the pair of fowlbeasts that make their nest in that tree outside taking turns to hunt and sit on their eggs. The eggs should hatch any day now.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I also saw the strange sight that was Tianshis of all vocations coming together to fret, even cry their hearts out before Shennong's statue...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The strangest scene I saw, however, was that of a few animals making a fool of a young kung fu master.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Did you find the stockbeast?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: When did you...?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Many years ago, the Grandmaster instructed me in the moves of all the various schools of kung fu and had me record the clashes with experts from those myriad schools. But my innate condition prevents me from studying the martial arts.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I said you must be exhausted, working in the fields by day and practicing kung fu by night. I envy you, as a matter of fact.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Even so, the Grandmaster allowed me to follow him, allowed someone who could not study kung fu to watch you do so.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: He didn't tell me what I was supposed to learn, only that I should pay attention to detail and accuracy. I recorded and studied according to his instructions.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Then I began to realize that kung fu isn't just about moves. The Grandmaster's philosophies on the fist are also philosophies on life, and every action or lack thereof corresponds to the natural laws of wax and wane.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: This wisdom amazed me even further, focusing on the infinite mysteries of kung fu. Where do you even start?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Sui Regulator's kung fu is not just for self-defense, but also to suppress the enemy and protect the innocent.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't think one should draw too many conclusions about it. It's just a skill.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Right. I later realized that it wasn't so complicated. Kung fu is just kung fu, no more, no less.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: I didn't learn this through study of the martial arts. I learned this wisdom from everyday life as I grew older and wiser, correlating it with kung fu.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Wisdom isn't about one thing. It's about everything.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Everything.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: The Grandmaster wrote in the Book of Arms, 'See the other through the self; remain upright and wait for the proper time.'

spans.text: , 'See the other through the self; remain upright and wait for the proper time.'

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: What he means is that one must ensure that one's posture is upright and firm, then seek the opportunity for victory.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: No matter the situation, one must remain composed, unaffected by outside matters...

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: What's that? You look like you saw a ghost.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: There you are, Candlestick! So you were with Inkbrush. I was looking for you all day!

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Rice Experiment Area A: Soil Originium activity was twenty percent during the growing period. Total production was approximately three hundred and twenty catties.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Experiment Area B: Twenty-three percent Originium activity, one hundred and fifty catties' production; Experiment Area C: Twenty-five percent Originium activity, almost zero crop survival...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Negligible change from last season's data, or the season before. The same goes for the other crop experiment areas.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: You don't look disappointed at all.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: No point trying to rush things. We take them one step at a time.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Twenty-five percent remains the critical line. Plant survivability drops off precipitously once soil Originium activity exceeds that level. This applies to both cash crops and cover crops.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Yet the figure remains much lower than the level of natural soil Originium activity in the vast majority of regions...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Thinking about giving up?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: No...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'm just not sure... if this is the only result, then there is no way to expand the application of the Wanqing 'the Ten Thousand Qing of Fertile Fields' project.

spans.text: I'm just not sure... if this is the only result, then there is no way to expand the application of the
'the Ten Thousand Qing of Fertile Fields' project.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: All these years, and nothing to show for it... not even a bud of hope.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Fifteen percent.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Twenty-five years ago, that was the critical line that had us stumped.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: It took nine generations of crops before we found an Originium-resistant variant in the corner of one of the plates.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: You and the Tianshis kept going for this long?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Did you know that people used to fertilize the fields with fluids from the Dahuang Fibrous Slug in order to protect crops from the impact of Originium?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Yes, but it's just folklore. There's no scientific basis to it. Originium doesn't infect plants like it does animals, it only changes the...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Yes, but that's what people in the past came up with when technology wasn't so advanced, the result of coincidence and misunderstanding.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: We tried so many different things, just to carve out a little piece of farmland for ourselves. It took generations after generations of trial and error to get agriculture to where it is today.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: As you said, the Wanqing project is one where hope is hard to come by.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Perhaps, many years later, people will look back at us the same way as we look back at the ancients who fertilized their fields with Fibrous Slug fluids.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Only one thing is clear, though. Plates on their own can't produce enough food for everyone. People will always go hungry in the remote villages, places where the nomadic city can't reach.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: And I'm willing to believe that, one day, we'll break the shackles of Originium, and then we'll truly have The Ten Thousand Qing of Fertile Fields... a certain someone said that to me, once upon a time.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Still working in the lab at this hour? The power bills keep piling up.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I-I'm just here to submit some data. I'll be going now!

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Oh, Xiaohe. Haven't seen you for a while. Look how tall you've grown! Why don't you stay for dinner?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Er, sorry, I, er, have things to do in the fields. Excuse me.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Why does he always look like he's terrified of me?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You're the big boss of Dahuang. People should be scared of you.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Doesn't mean everyone will listen to me. Isn't the hour a little late to still be working?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Alright, alright, I'll be going.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Cooking soup so late is rather tiring.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Mm, smells good.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Who are you treating? Your sisters? Or that 'relative' of yours who came to visit? What's his name, Zuo Le?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Everyone's working hard in preparation for the summer harvest. This soup is for the hardest worker.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Did you have to poke fun at me before dinner? A little mean, don't you think?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Then bring the bowl over.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: All my life I've been dealing with things that grow from the soil. Now I have to learn everything about engineering from scratch.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: And it's not easy, dealing with the Ministry of Works, arguing all day about the assignment of a few Tianshis. It's even more tiring than farmwork.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Eat up, then. You've definitely lost a few catties.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Sure. Except...

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Three huge pieces of rib in one bowl? You're trying to burst my stomach.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Three's plenty. One more and it's going to spill over.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Spilled soup would make a mess, and it's even worse when someone gets burned.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You can put it down if you don't want it.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: That won't do. So much effort went into this soup, we can't let it go to waste.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Do you have to talk like that today?

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: I'm just talking about this bowl of ribs and lian'ou soup.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: The ribs come from lovingly raised meatbeasts, while the lian'ou comes from ponds that we dug with our own hands.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: This soup represents the efforts of generations of people, and of your efforts all these years. We must not allow what should not be here to ruin this hard-won soil.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: After all these years, you...

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: So many years. I've almost forgotten how I came to know you.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Sometimes I wish I really did. If only you were just a diligent Nongye Tianshi, and me a humble farmer.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: But I could never forget. Even if I forgot, someone would help me remember. The scrolls of the Sui Regulator remember. The list of fallen Candleholders remembers.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Say no more.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: You know what I mean. What I'm concerned about. Your... 'brother'.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: One person can fool another, but no one can fool time. It took me the better part of my lifetime to come to trust you. I don't have the time left to trust another.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: He shouldn't have come back at a time like this, Shu.

steps.name: Old Xiangzhang
steps.text: Don't make things difficult for me.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Good evening, Grain Buds.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Inkbrush... why are you standing so far away?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Alright, I promise, I know your book isn't a sketchbook and I won't add faces to the people in it.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: (Sketchbook? Does she mean your Record of Martial Combat?)

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: (My fault.)

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: (Don't ever let the Grandmaster or Qiubai see it.)

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: (I know...)

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: (Although, come to think of it, they might like the cartoonish style...)

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Ahem...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Were you looking for me, Grain Buds?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Here, this is for you.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: A bracelet?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Weaved from Mianmian's wool. Thank-you gift for bringing him home today.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I didn't do anything... except cause problems.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Well, don't think too much about what Xiaohe said. He's alright most of the time, but he gets all angry and stubborn when it comes to farming. All the young Tianshis he tutors are scared of him.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: He's already a Shouye Tianshi?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: I think? He takes over Shu's lessons when she's busy. There are so many kinds of Tianshi, I just can't keep track of them.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Say, why are you called Candlestick, anyway?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Candleholder?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Yeah! It's so weird. Nobody uses candles anymore.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The title 'Candleholder' comes from...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Never mind. It means that I'm one of Yan's official Messengers.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Well, mind that you don't accidentally set the letters on fire.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Pfft.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What are you snickering at, sketchbook Inkbrush?

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Nothing, Candlestick messenger.
The sky grows dark. The summer breeze brings the fresh scent of the earth.
Insects sing amongst the grass as the stars rise.
There is a figure wandering not far away, and Grain Buds picks it up right away.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Xiaohe! When are you gonna come over?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Are you still angry that I asked you to help get the Tianshis to register the foals?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'm not angry.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'm just exhausted after dealing with the foals he brought back.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Oh... do you need to go to bed?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: And we need to name the pair. They were found together... I've got an idea! Let's name them Xiaoman like 'Grain Buds' and Xiaohe like 'Grain Stalk'!

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: No way.
He Sheng sits down on the grass.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Sorry. If you're still angry at me.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'm not really angry at you...

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Candlestick! What is a Messenger like you doing in Dahuang? You're not delivering letters, just playing with us all day.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I made a mistake. Father sent me here to learn.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But I'm still not sure what I'm supposed to learn, or how I'm supposed to learn it.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: In my old job, there were a lot of things that hadn't been cleared up, but Father wouldn't let me investigate. I'm not even sure what I'm doing here...

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Wow, your dad's scary.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: When the teachers at the Tianshi Bureau scold the kids even younger than me, they say that if you don't behave, your baba and mama will come and punish you.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Well, Candlestick got punished by his baba. But I've made so many mistakes, so why don't my baba and mama come and punish me?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Your parents...?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Shu says my parents are Tianshis in a place far away. But she never told me what they do, or why I don't hear from them.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: The Xiangzhang says my parents named me Xiaoman, or Grain Buds, because they think we should be content with the little things, like grains in the field.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: General Zuo must be hoping that you'll live a happy and carefree life, Zuo Le.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Grandmaster must hope that you will be content and comfortable in whatever situation then, Yun.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Come to think of it, I never got the chance to ask you your name.

steps.name: Record Keeper
steps.text: Yun Qingping. People sometimes say it sounds like a girl's name.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Not at all. It's nice.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Reminds me of lotus ponds in summer.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Xiaohe's name has a story behind it too! The farmers found him in the rice fields. The old folks thought he was born from the rice crops, which is how he got a name that means rice stalk.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Shu still has a picture from back then! I'll bring it tomorrow.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Grain Buds!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Everyone loves that photo. Candlestick and Inkbrush should see it too!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: (Why doesn't He Sheng get a nickname beyond Xiaohe?)

steps.name: Yun Qingping
steps.text: (Why not contribute one? Grain Buds here seems quite amendable to suggestions.)
The summer evening breeze brushes their hair, to the accompaniment of cicada songs.
A few fireflies take to the air, while stars fall from the sky.
Grain Buds is no longer chasing the fireflies. She sits on the grass smelling of night dew, panting from the chase.
There is no room for gloom or worry in the heart of the young and innocent. She only has eyes for the sincere joy of the present.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Look! Shooting stars!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: According to Shu, the old Shennong stories say that crops grow well where the shooting star falls.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Should we go and see where they fell?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: She said that to get you to come down from your tree and go to bed. You seriously think it's true?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Of course I do!

steps.name: Yun Qingping
steps.text: But it's very far away, way beyond Dahuang.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Then we'll leave Dahuang.

steps.name: Yun Qingping
steps.text: What if they fell at the edge of Heaven?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Then we'll go to the edge of Heaven! I'll go. You'll come too, Xiaohe, and the rest of you, too.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: There's a lot of time to look for them before the sun rises.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Maybe we'll never find them, and keep walking until we're all grandpas and grandmas.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Searching for stars?

steps.name: Yun Qingping
steps.text: Hah, yes, searching for stars.

steps.name: Yun Qingping
steps.text: Has it occurred to you that this may be what you're supposed to be looking for?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Stars?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Come, let's cross this stream!

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Hey, Zuo Le.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: How old are you?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Nineteen.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Nothing... I'm older than you.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Wei, what are you talking about over there?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Tomorrow is the Xiazhi. Dahuang will be holding the Shennong Festival, welcoming Shennong with songs and costumes. Let's go have some fun!

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Didn't you say you wanted to look for the stars?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: I said, until the sun rises.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Shennong Festival? That's not for fun, is it?

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Of course it is! They put on plays and fairs, and there's lots to eat! The Xiangzhang says everybody has been working so hard, we should relax a little.

steps.name: Grain Buds
steps.text: Xiaohe's going. I'm gonna play the flute... there are other shows too!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Alright, I'll go and see.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I'll see... and think.
